0.content: Petronilla, a Marechaussee Hunter, raised Clorinde from early childhood and trained her as a Hunter. She claimed to have rescued the abandoned child "from people of ill repute". She knew little about children and believed in trial and error: a real short sword as a first toy, a Geovishap Hatchling as a pet with the rule "whoever loses is the real pet", blindfolded drills in the woods. Clorinde never heard her mention her own parents, and later concluded she simply knew no other way to raise a child. Strict and powerful, she was also playful and impulsive; she took Clorinde travelling to meet friends, among them Callas. By night she was the black-cloaked vigilante "Protector of Justice" (or "of Order"; she reportedly made up names on the spot), wanted on posters and the subject of Gardes reports on Neuvillette's desk about twenty years ago. On the night Clorinde turned ten she vanished without a note.

1.content: Navia, now boss of the Spina di Rosula, met Clorinde when she was a little over ten and Clorinde was a shy child hiding behind Petronilla at a picnic. Clorinde became a regular at the Spina, won shooting contests against its members, and hosted Navia's endless tabletop adventures. After Clorinde killed Callas, the two could not face each other for years; Navia felt she had lost a father and a friend. Clorinde quietly followed her to keep her safe, rescued her and the Traveler from rogue Gardemeks, and helped reveal Callas's real motive. Now they are close again. Navia drags her to the Tabletop Troupe, tries to cheat with explosives and krumkake, and is overruled every time.

2.content: Callas, founder of the Spina di Rosula and Navia's father, was Petronilla's friend and welcomed Clorinde into his home. Three years before the Traveler reached Fontaine, the Sinthe ring led by Marcel framed him for murder. Testifying in court would have exposed Navia to their revenge, so he demanded a duel against Clorinde instead and asked her to keep his daughter safe. He refused to yield even when badly wounded; under her code of honour that meant the duel ended in his death. Clorinde can tell when someone fights to live and when they fight to die. She kept his request, shadowing Navia for years, and in 4.0 told her: "Mr. Callas' last wish was for me to ensure your safety, and I will not betray his trust."

3.content: Clorinde served as Furina's bodyguard and was at her side when the Traveler arrived in Fontaine. When a crowd assumed the Traveler had come to duel the Archon, Clorinde moved to intercept until Furina waved her down. In 4.2 she was stationed at the Opera Epiclese, ready to duel Furina if she refused trial; Furina chose the trial. The duel challenge made Clorinde so famous that she had to lie low in Poisson. Now, she says, she sits at Furina's tea table instead of standing behind it, and is starting to understand why Furina complains about keeping her figure. Furina trusts her and plans to invite her to tea parties.

4.content: After ancient Remuria fell, monsters plagued Fontaine. Answering Egeria's call, Cassiodor the "Golden Hunter" gathered ordinary mortal warriors (descendants of the Lochknights among them) into the Marechaussee Hunters. Their only advantage was sword techniques handed down through the generations. As Fontaine grew peaceful they faded into legend, and the Marechaussee Phantom they founded became mostly Melusine. Most Fontainians know only the Hunter's Oath from plays and novels; it begins "From this day, I pass the candle's shadow-veil" and ends "And so shall I never despair." To Clorinde it is a living inheritance, though she wants to be recognised only as a Champion Duelist.

5.comment: Clorinde: Champion Duelists and trial by combat
5.content: In Fontaine, a party who thinks a verdict unjust may ask to settle it by a duel against a Champion Duelist appointed by the court. It gives people a chance to defend their honour and to be heard. Clorinde calls the job simple: defeat the opponent as the Trial Court requests. Some call her an "executioner". Her name alone ends many petty disputes: when a Gestionnaire mentions that the duelist on the roster is Miss Clorinde, publicity-seeking litigants suddenly decide there is no need to go that far. Most of her opponents now surrender, and more did after she received her Vision. She finds it absurd when people bring disputes like whether Marcotte belongs in coffee to the point of swords.

6.content: The Tabletop Troupe is a roleplaying adventure club in the Court of Fontaine; players take characters in a script and use the Fateometer for checks. Clorinde is one of its few Senior Game Masters. She came in with Navia, terrifying the owner, who nearly said "Please, have mercy!" instead of "Welcome!" As a player she missed no clue and kept every rule. She went back to running games largely to spare the club's other GMs from Navia's imagination. She cannot be bribed with cake, fries or Bulle Fruit. She likes GMing because she can watch people react to a world she controls without getting caught up in the drama, but insists it is not like watching caged prey: she just wants the players to enjoy the story.
